# Psalm 49 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Of-the-sons of-Korah. A-psalm.

**2** Hear this, all-the-peoples; give-ear, all inhabitants of-the-world,

**3** both low and-high, rich and-poor together.

**4** My-mouth speaks wisdom, and-the-meditation of-my-heart [is] understanding.

**5** I-incline my-ear to-a-proverb; I-open with-the-lyre my-riddle.

**6** Why should-I-fear in-days of-evil, [when] the-iniquity of-my-heels [of those at my heels] surrounds-me?

**7** Those-trusting in-their-wealth and-in-the-abundance of-their-riches they-boast —

**8** surely a-man cannot ransom a-brother; he-cannot give to-God his-ransom-price —

**9** for costly [is] the-ransom of-their-soul, and-it-ceases forever —

**10** that he-should-live on forever [and] not see the-pit.

**11** For he-sees [that] wise-men die; together the-fool and-the-stupid perish and-leave to-others their-wealth.

**12** Their-graves [are] their-homes forever, their-dwelling-places to-all generations, [though] they-called [lands] by-their-names.

**13** But-man in-honor does-not endure; he-is-like the-beasts [that] perish.

**14** This [is] the-way of-those-who-are-foolish, and-of-their-followers who-delight in-their-words. Selah.

**15** Like-sheep they-are-appointed for-Sheol; death shepherds-them, and-the-upright rule-over-them in-the-morning, and-their-form [is for] Sheol to-consume, far-from-their-dwelling.

**16** But God ransoms my-soul from-the-hand of-Sheol, for He-takes-me. Selah.

**17** Do-not fear when-a-man grows-rich, when-the-glory of-his-house increases;

**18** for at-his-death he-takes nothing; his-glory does-not go-down after-him.

**19** Though in-his-lifetime he-blesses his-soul — and-they-praise-you when-you-do-well for-yourself —

**20** he goes to-the-generation of-his-fathers; they never see light.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **49:16**: The verb 'takes me' (yiqqacheni) is the same used for Enoch (Gen 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3). God 'takes' the righteous beyond death's reach.

— EMET
